Duties and Privileges of the Leader of the Opposition

statement · 31 August 2020 · 41 sentences in the record

Duties and Privileges of the Leader of the Opposition

32 of 41 sentences in this record
Ms Indranee Rajah
Leader of Opposition not in Constitution

The Leader of the Opposition role is not provided for in the Constitution or Parliament's Standing Orders.

  2. s00003 · ministerial-statement-1446Ms Indranee Rajah

    The position of the Leader of the Opposition is not provided for in our Constitution or in the Standing Orders of Parliament.

    • Ms Indranee Rajah
    Seat, resources and first response

    The Opposition leader sits opposite the Prime Minister and gets an office, staff, resources, allowance and first response rights.

    1. s00011 · ministerial-statement-1446Ms Indranee Rajahcontext

      The leader of the main Opposition party typically takes the seat directly opposite the Prime Minister in this Chamber during Parliament sittings, similar to the practice in other countries that formally recognise the role of the Leader of the Opposition.

    2. s00012 · ministerial-statement-1446Ms Indranee Rajah

      He will be given an office in Parliament, staff support and resources and additional allowance.

    3. s00013 · ministerial-statement-1446Ms Indranee Rajah

      The Leader of the Opposition will generally be given the right of first response among MPs to ask the lead question of Ministers on policies, Bills and Motions in Parliament.

    • Ms Indranee Rajah
    Pritam Singh's Opposition duties

    As Leader of the Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh leads and organises Opposition parliamentary business, including alternative views, scrutiny and committee nominations.

    1. s00019 · ministerial-statement-1446Ms Indranee Rajahcontext

      As Leader of the Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh will lead and organise the Opposition's parliamentary business.

    2. s00020 · ministerial-statement-1446Ms Indranee Rajah

      This includes leading the Opposition in: (a) Presenting alternative views in parliamentary debates on policies, Bills and Motions; (b) Scrutinising the Government’s positions and actions in Parliament; and (c) Nominating Opposition Members for appointment to Select Committees, including Standing Select Committees such as the Public Accounts Committee.

    • Mr Speaker
    First response and longer speeches

    Where practices allow, the Leader of the Opposition has first response rights and, with House agreement, longer speaking duration, supported by extra staff and resources.

    1. s00036 · ministerial-statement-1446Mr Speaker

      Where the existing practices and conventions allow, the Leader of the Opposition will have the right of first response amongst Members to pose lead questions to Ministers.

    2. s00037 · ministerial-statement-1446Mr Speaker

      Subject to the agreement of the House, he will also be granted longer speaking duration for speeches.

    4. s00039 · ministerial-statement-1446Mr Speaker

      The additional staff and resources provided to him would support the Leader of the Opposition in this endeavour.

    A 2016 constitutional commission chaired by the Chief Justice recommended ways to ensure multiracial representation in the Elected President office, noting a race-blind community as the ultimate destination.

      In its report, the commission noted as follows and I quote, "The ultimate destination for our society should be a race-blind community where no safeguards are required to ensure that candidates from different ethnic groups and periodically elected into presidential office.

    Scope of race review

    The speaker lists six areas for a review, including CMIO classifications, race-based data disclosure, self-help groups, multiracialism in elections and HDB's Ethnic Integration Policy.

    1. s00092 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sylvia Lim — Aljunied

      As for the scope of such a review, I can suggest that the following be considered: one, the relevance of existing ethnic classifications such as CMIO; two, the scope for more public disclosure of race-based data; three, how not to reinforce tribal instincts in public policies and surveys; four, whether the current self-help groups should be amalgamated within a unifying national body to pool national resources on a race-blind basis; five, whether multiracialism in elections should be preserved under the current framework or can less intrusive methods be used; and six, whether HDB’s Ethnic Integration Policy should be retained and if so, how it can be modified for fairness.

    Triple Uplift for low-wage workers

    Singapore helps low-wage workers through a Triple Uplift formula of Progressive Wage Model, Workfare Income Supplement and National Wage Council recommendations.

    1. s00587 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Dr Koh Poh Koon

      In Singapore, our way of helping the low-wage workers is via, what I will call, the “Triple Uplift” formula: Progressive Wage Model or PWM, plus Workfare Income Supplement or WIS, and, of course, National Wage Council (NWC) recommendations – using all these three – to uplift their wages.

    • Dr Koh Poh Koon
    Wage growth of lowest percentile

    Through the Triple Uplift formula, wages of the lowest 20th percentile grew 4.4% annually from 2014 to 2019, compared to 2.3% in the preceding five years.

    1. s00590 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Dr Koh Poh Koon

    1. s00602 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Dr Koh Poh Koon

    With overtime pay and AWS or bonuses this could be higher, but these three sectors account for about 78,000 workers, about 15% of the lowest 20th percentile.

    1. s03658 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      Whether it be the strong support from the SG United Jobs and Skills Package, the new Jobs Growth Incentive or efforts from the Tripartite Committee on Employability of Older Workers.

    Job redesign for mature workforce

    1. s03664 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      To begin with, I have helped to bring together the NCSS and Pan Pacific Hotel Group to start dialogues on partnership to join forces and combine the social and business perspectives to enable awareness and resources for new job redesigns for the mature workforce.

    3. s03666 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      For example, the hotel group in their sustainability pursuit are thinking of new roles such as urban farming specialists where they will encourage older workers to pursue and in a dignified way.

    • Ms Ng Ling Ling
    Surveys on older adults' wellbeing

    Surveys reported in The Straits Times found older adults' life satisfaction dropped and social isolation and anxiety rose during the period.

    1. s03672 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kiocontext

      The findings from their population-representative monthly survey, with about 7,500 respondents, tracking the lives of Singaporeans aged 55 to 75 during this period were reported in The Straits Times on 28 August this year.

    2. s03673 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      There was an important finding: older adults experienced a drop in overall life satisfaction by 3.8% in April 2020 and 4% in May, as compared to January 2020.

    3. s03674 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      Respondents mentioned that they experienced a sharp increase in feelings of social isolation, with individuals living alone experiencing larger increases.

    4. s03675 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      One factor that impacts quality of life is job security, and it is telling that many respondents in the survey expressed anxiety about the future, with about a third of respondents expressing being very or extremely worried about the health of their loved ones and the economy.

    6. s03677 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      In another survey conducted by the National University Health System (NUHS) Mind Science Centre on mental health resilience published in The Straits Times on 19 August this year, it found that younger Singaporeans 45 years and below are more likely to feel anxious and less mentally resilient than those aged 45 and above.

    • Ms Ng Ling Ling
    Preventive mental health support

    1. s03685 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kiocontext

      We must continue to reduce the stigma of help seeking behaviours for Singaporeans, especially when it is at the early onset of mental health issues, such as mild depression or anxiety, for preventive care nearer to home in the community.

    2. s03686 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Ng Ling Ling — Ang Mo Kio

      I hope to encourage more preventive mental health support in primary care providers, including the polyclinics and general practitioner (GP) clinics, which are closer to most people, with more support in terms of subsidies and integrated care with social services.

    • Mr Eric Chua
    MSF income mobility paper

    A 2018 MSF paper found 14.3% of Singaporeans born 1978-1982 to lowest-income families reached the top 20%.

    1. s03719 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Eric Chua

      According to a 2018 paper published by the MSF, 14.3% of Singaporeans born between 1978 and 1982 to families from the lowest 20% in terms of household income made it to the top 20%, significantly higher than other developed countries, like the US and the UK.

    2. s03720 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Eric Chua

      Families who make up this statistic are completely uplifted in a single generation.

    ASPIRE, UPLIFT, KidSTART efforts

    1. s03730 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Eric Chua

    2. s03770 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Eric Chua

    Live telecast of Parliament

    A spokesman said live broadcasts risk turning Parliament into theatre and do not add transparency, but the Member agrees to live telecast.

    1. s03809 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

      A spokesman for Minister Grace Fu, responding to this through the media, said "Live broadcasts of Parliament risk turning the House into a ‘form of theatre’ and do not add to transparency", and further said, "An element of public performance is unavoidable because Singaporeans want to see their concerns expressed, and hear their questions asked and answered in Parliament." In short, the answer given is that the live telecast does not improve transparency; in fact, it poses a risk of transforming Parliamentary sessions into performance theatre.

    2. s03810 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

      On this note, Sir, I would like to state for the record that I agree to having live telecast of Parliamentary sessions, because in my view, any Member who wants to put on a theatre performance in Parliament will still showcase their acting because they know that, although there is no live telecast, there are recordings done every second, from the start to the end of the Parliamentary session.

    2. s03822 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

    PA grassroots advisers proposal

    Explanations failed to convince observers, and the Member proposed appointing non-partisan senior public officers as PA grassroots advisers.

    1. s03826 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

    2. s03827 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljuniedcontext

      While the individual and family must continue to be cardinal and first line of support, we also need stronger interventions – by Government, local communities and society at large – to support families in providing dignified care for our seniors.

    Government bearing care costs

    Higher care standards raise costs, and the Government should bear the bulk of incremental costs and review the subsidy framework.

    1. s03871 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurongcontext

      To raise and sustain an ecosystem of capability building, innovation and human capital development, cost of care in the sector would have to go up.

    2. s03872 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      I believe there is scope for the Government to bear the bulk of incremental costs for these higher standards of care.

    3. s03873 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      At the same time, while most nursing home residents are already getting some level of Government subsidies, I would urge a review of the current subsidy framework to see if we can do more and be even more progressive.

    • Mr Xie Yao Quan
    Flattening healthcare cost inflation

    As the population ages, healthcare spending demands grow, so the healthcare cost inflation curve must be flattened.

    1. s03877 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurongcontext

    2. s03878 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      Therefore, while we keep at flattening the epidemic and unemployment curves in the COVID-19 new normal, we must also urgently flatten our healthcare cost inflation curve.

    1. s03896 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      Indeed, we need to grow our home-based care capabilities in a major way, including the protocols, technology, financing and regulations.

    Care remains high-touch, so more nurses are needed, maintaining a strong Singaporean Core while complementing the workforce with foreign nurses.

    1. s03900 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurongcontext

      We continue to improve productivity through technology and job redesign, but fundamentally, care remains a high-touch, highly human endeavour, especially if we want care to be dignified.

    2. s03901 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      We need more nurses going forward and it is key that we maintain a strong Singaporean Core.

    3. s03902 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

    4. s03903 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      But we also need to complement our workforce with foreign nurses.

    Dependency Ratio Ceiling healthcare review

    The speaker suggests a comprehensive review of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling and manpower strategies for the healthcare sector, especially intermediate and long-term care.

    1. s03915 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      To this end, I would also suggest a comprehensive review of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling and manpower strategies for the healthcare sector, especially for intermediate and long-term care.

    • Mr Xie Yao Quan
    Three suggestions for eldercare

    The speaker makes three suggestions: build nursing homes and raise subsidies, explore home care services, and give caregivers financial help and parent care leave.

    1. s03935 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      Here I have three suggestions: first, the Government should focus on developing and building nursing homes, inject more resources, improve the quality of care beyond basic care, and at the same time increase subsidies for Singaporeans; second, explore more comprehensive home care services because hospital wards can never be as comfortable as a bedroom at home; and third, provide more financial assistance to full-time caregivers and establish a suitable parent care leave regime through the Tripartite partners.

    • Mr Xie Yao Quan · Mr Chan Chun Sing
    Dignified care for seniors

    The speaker says hard choices on treatments are needed to limit costs, more people must provide care, and society must care for caregivers and seniors.

    1. s03944 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      At the same time, we need to make hard choices on treatments and therapies and involve our tertiary care model to keep a lid on overall costs.

    2. s03945 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      Yet, overall costs would go up and these would have to be funded.

    3. s03946 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurongcontext

      And certainly, our society would need more passionate individuals, both local and foreign, to step forward to provide the best care possible for our seniors.

    4. s03947 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      And finally, as a society, we must also care better for our caregivers.

    5. s03948 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      We must be a society that commits to dignified care for our seniors, because it is the right thing to do.

    6. s03949 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Xie Yao Quan — Jurong

      And we must be a society that commits to stepping in and stepping up to help each other with the burdens of care, especially where the individual or the family is unable to manage, because this is who we must be as a people.

    2. s03955 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Chan Chun Sing

    KidSTART support for lower income families

    1. s03989 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xuelingcontext

      They say it takes a village to raise a child.

    2. s03990 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xueling

      I hope that with the scale-up of programmes such as KidSTART, which provides holistic support to lower income families and focus on the health, nutrition and education of their children, more of these children and their families can benefit.

    • Ms Sun Xueling
    Education system mindset shift

    The education system is reducing assessments and changing PSLE scoring, but society, employers and parents must also shift away from overemphasising grades, with DSA changes ensuring holistic assessment.

    1. s03995 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xueling

      Our education system has been making big moves to bring about a mindset shift to look beyond academic achievements, by reducing school-based assessments and making changes to the PSLE scoring system.

    2. s03996 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xuelingcontext

      But to do this successfully, we all need to move away from an overemphasis on grades, not just within the school system but a broader mindset shift in society, including from among employers and parents.

    3. s03997 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xueling

      And we need to make real changes to some of the current ways of doing things, such as a greater recognition of skills when evaluating someone for a job.

    5. s03999 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xuelingcontext

      But even as we do so, we must be careful not to rely solely on tried-and-tested methods, such as assessing students based on certificates which show demonstrated achievements.

    6. s04000 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xueling

      This would only serve to transfer the competition for results from the academic arena to the non-academic arena, with better off parents being more likely to send their children for extra training in DSA areas.

    7. s04001 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xueling

      Instead, we have started making changes to DSA over the past few years, and parents and children can be assured that our schools are adopting a much more holistic assessment, looking beyond past achievements.

    4. s04027 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xueling

    • Ms Sun Xueling
    COVID-19 impact on families and marriages

    Teenagers may be in low spirits staying home, family violence enquiries rose about 10% during circuit breaker, and marriages from January to July dropped 23%.

    1. s04039 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Ms Sun Xuelingcontext

      Teenagers may be in low spirits as they must stay at home for long periods and are unable to meet their friends as and when they like.

    • Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
    Declaring EP holders' country of origin

    Proposes mandating large companies with over 25% EP holders to declare EP holders' country of origin across four annual remuneration bands.

    1. s07153 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry — Kebun Baru

      One way is to mandate all companies with more than 200 staff and with more than 25% EP holders to declare the country of origin of their EP holders along four annual renumeration bands: one, from $60,000 to $120,000 a year; two, from $120,000 to $250,000; from $250,000 to $500,000; and beyond $500,000.

    2. s07154 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry — Kebun Baru

      After all, if the EP holders are dominated by one particular country, despite our very diverse expatriate workforce, how can Singaporeans be persuaded that there is diversity in these companies’ hiring and renumeration policy, and how can Singaporeans trust that they have a genuine intention to build up a Singapore Core?

    1. s08545 · president-address-1448+1452+1454+1456+1459+1461+1466+1468+1478Mr Desmond Lee
